in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child I'm responsible for. I'm asking about one child - my son Alex. He's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have an 11-year-old son named Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Do you make regular financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or housing)? And if so, how much do you contribute?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with things like clothes and essentials. I give £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you but you're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep, I need to clarify:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and has anyone else claimed Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum. As far as I know, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more important question:

**Are you and Alex's mum married or in a civil partnership and living together, or are you living separately?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: We're living separately - we're not together anymore.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

While Alex is 11 years old (which meets the age requirement of under 16), and you do contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit amount), the key issue is that **only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child**.

Since Alex lives with his mum and you are living separately, she would be the person who qualifies for Child Benefit as the primary caregiver. When parents are separated and the child lives with one parent, that parent is the one who should claim Child Benefit.

If his mum isn't currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, she would be the appropriate person to make the claim. Your financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep are important for his welfare, but they don't make you eligible to claim Child Benefit when he's living with his other parent.

However, according to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify if you're responsible for a child, which usually means either: (1) you live with them, or (2) you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them. Alex does not live with you - he lives with his mum. While you contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep, the current Child Benefit rate for the first child is £25.60 per week (2024/25 rate), so your contribution does meet the threshold amount. However, the rules clearly state that only ONE person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex lives with his mum and you are living separately (not married/civil partnered and living together), his mum would be the person who qualifies for Child Benefit as she is the primary caregiver with whom Alex resides. If no one is currently claiming, his mum would be the appropriate person to make the claim, not you. Therefore, you are ineligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex in these circumstances.
